item.title: Delta: Police arrest school bus driver over alleged kidnap, assault of 14-year-old
item.description: By Emmauel Okogba The Delta State Police Command has arrested a 28-year-old school bus driver, Onome Lucky Ughagha, over the alleged kidnapping and sexual assault of a 14-year-old female student in Sapele. The suspect was also accused of demanding and collecting ₦503,000 from the victim’s father as ransom before abandoning the girl along Oton Road, Sapele. The police said the incident was reported at the Sapele Area Command on October 20, 2026, by the victim’s father, who alleged that the suspect abducted his daughter while she was preparing to leave for school. According to a statement by the Police Public Relations Officer, Delta State Command, SP Bright Edafe, the suspect allegedly contacted the girl’s father, demanded ₦503,000 and threatened to kill the minor if the money was not paid. The statement said the victim was abandoned along Oton Road after the ransom was paid and subsequently reunited with her family in a traumatised condition, with indications that she had been sexually assaulted. Following the report, operatives of the Sapele Area Command commenced investigations, while the victim was taken to a medical facility for examination and treatment. The police added that the school principal and vice principal were invited for questioning as efforts intensified to apprehend the suspect, who had allegedly abandoned the school bus and fled. Edafe said the suspect was eventually arrested on October 23 at his hideout in the Ajimele area of Sapele following intelligence-led operations. “During preliminary interrogation, he reportedly confessed to his involvement in the crime,” the statement said. The police disclosed that arrangements were underway to transfer the suspect to the State Criminal Investigation Department in Asaba for further investigation. The Commissioner of Police in Delta State, CP Samuel Erale, condemned the incident and reaffirmed the command’s commitment to protecting children from violence and exploitation. He assured that the investigation would be thorough and that anyone found culpable would be brought to justice. The commissioner also urged school authorities, parents and transport operators to strengthen measures to protect children, stressing that the safety of every child entrusted to their care must remain a priority. item.description: President Emmanuel Macron said on Monday that social media was “damaging our democracies” as France struggled to contain weeks of protests marked by street violence and looting. He said on a visit to Marseille that social media was especially used during unrest on October 17 “to bring young and not-so-young people to places where criminal acts, attacks and looting were taking place”. item.description: Ondo State House of Assembly has passed a bill seeking to amend the 1999 Constitution to provide for the establishment of state police services. The bill was passed following deliberations by the lawmakers at a plenary session on Monday in Akure. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the proposal was conveyed to the assembly in a letter from the National Assembly Clerk, Kamoru Ogunlana, which was read by the Speaker, Olamide Oladiji, on Sept. 24. The House Leader, Olatunji Oshati, who moved for the passage and its transmission to the National Assembly, said the lawmakers had considered the implications of the proposed amendment for the citizenry. Oshati said that the establishment of state police would address the numerous security challenges confronting the country. The motion was seconded by Mr Allen Oluwatoyin, All Progressives Congress (APC), member representing Ese-Odo State Constituency. Also speaking, Oladiji described the proposed establishment of state police as long overdue, saying it would enable security agencies to respond more swiftly to crime and other security concerns. He noted that state policing, being grassroots-based, would reduce crime through improved intelligence gathering and proactive security measures. “There will be greater confidence in state policing. It will strengthen intelligence gathering and provide grassroots security,” he added. The speaker, however, commended the lawmakers for their contributions to the bill and its passage. It was gathered that the bill would be transmitted to the National Assembly for further legislative consideration. Moments later a chorus of boos erupted as the players left the pitch — with fans clear in their minds where the blame lies for United’s current malaise. Carrick was handed a two-year deal in May after inspiring an impressive revival following the team’s struggles under Ruben Amorim — United secured third place in the Premier League and a return to the Champions League. But a drastic decline this season is an all-too-familiar story for United supporters, who last witnessed a Premier League title triumph 13 years ago under Alex Ferguson. Carrick, 45, is clinging on but his position appears increasingly precarious, with former Newcastle boss Eddie Howe and ex-Germany boss Julian Nagelsmann apparently in the frame for the job. item.title: US singer Chris Brown avoids jail over UK nightclub brawl
item.description: American R&B singer Chris Brown avoided jail when sentenced by a UK court Monday after pleading guilty to a public order offence during a 2023 brawl at a London nightclub. The former boyfriend of music sensation Rihanna was handed an eight-month jail sentence suspended for a year — meaning he will not be imprisoned unless he commits another offence during the period. Brown, 37, who was wearing a black face mask and black cap when he arrived Monday at Southwark Crown Court in London, had admitted to affray during an appearance in July. “Violence of this kind in a crowded nightclub is serious. It creates an obvious risk, not merely to the person against whom it is directed, but also to others,” judge Tony Baumgartner said, handing down the sentence. Prosecutors had accused him and co-defendant Omololu Akinlolu, also a US national, of carrying out “a vicious and unprovoked attack” in a crowded nightclub “where Brown used a glass bottle as a weapon to strike the victim’s head twice”. The guilty plea avoided a trial on several other charges, including attempting to cause grievous bodily harm with intent and possession of an offensive weapon, namely a bottle. Brown, who has sold tens of millions of records worldwide, had earlier denied those charges. All of the allegations relate to an incident at Tape, a private members’ club in central London, on February 19, 2023, while Brown was touring the UK. The victim was struck several times with a bottle before being pursued, punched and kicked. The singer is known for mid-2000s hits such as “Kiss, Kiss”, as well as a litany of legal troubles including a felony conviction for assaulting Rihanna in 2009. Brown rose from a local church choir in Virginia to sudden fame with his rich R&B voice before turning to rap. He was convicted of having beaten then-girlfriend Rihanna before the 2009 Grammy Awards, forcing the pop star to miss the annual gala. In 2012, Brown was involved in an altercation at a New York nightclub with members of hip hop star Drake’s entourage, during which French basketball player Tony Parker suffered an eye injury after being hit by a thrown glass bottle. Two years later, Brown pleaded guilty to assaulting a fan in Washington. Akinlolu, 40 also pleaded guilty to affray over the London incident. He was sentenced to four months’ imprisonment suspended for a year. The post US singer Chris Brown avoids jail over UK nightclub brawl appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi has demanded the release of party supporter Rilwan Olawale, accusing President Bola Tinubu of undermining democracy by “encouraging and facilitating violence.” In a statement posted on X on Monday, Obi described the reported incident as part of what he called the intimidation and harassment of his supporters. He also accused President Bola Tinubu of encouraging and facilitating violence, and demanded transparency over Olawale’s reported arrest, respect for his rights and an end to what he described as politically motivated harassment. “The continued intimidation and harassment of my supporters across the country, the latest being the case of Rilwan Olawale, is disturbing and unacceptable. “President Bola Tinubu has remained a huge beneficiary of our democracy and should not brazenly be destroying it by encouraging and facilitating violence.” Obi further stated that his campaign was peaceful and issue-driven, and warned that his supporters’ restraint should not be mistaken for weakness. “We have chosen the path of peace, not violence; persuasion, not intimidation. item.title: Trump blasts Norway over Nobel Peace Prize snub
item.description: US President Donald Trump attacked Norway during a campaign rally, calling it a “shit house country,” and said that Norwegian immigrants were not welcome in the United States because its Nobel Committee had not awarded him the Peace Prize. “Frankly, Norway sucks. Norway has become a shit house country, actually,” he said during Sunday’s speech. Since returning to the White House in January 2025, Trump has made no secret of his desire to win the prestigious Nobel Peace prize. Judge and former UN rights chief Navi Pillay of South Africa was this year’s recipient of the prize. Trump has called the committee’s choice “a disgraceful and embarrassing decision” and argued that the award should have gone to him. Trump said Sunday he would welcome immigrants from certain countries but not Norway “because I didn’t get the Nobel Prize.” “So I don’t want anybody from Norway,” he said during the rally in the Michigan town of Port Huron ahead of crucial US midterm elections on November 3. There was no official indication of a new US policy on Norwegian immigrants. Norwegian Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide responded to Trump’s comments about the Nobel prize on Monday, maintaining that the committee is independent. “He knows very well that the Nobel Committee is independent. We have reminded him of that, in case anyone is wondering – and that is still the case,” he told national broadcaster NRK. Trump came under fire in 2018, during his first term, after using similar vulgar expressions to refer to Haiti and certain African countries. Since returning to the White House in January 2025, Trump has made no secret of his desire to win the prestigious Nobel Peace prize. Judge and former UN rights chief Navi Pillay of South Africa was this year’s recipient of the prize. Trump has called the committee’s choice “a disgraceful and embarrassing decision” and argued that the award should have gone to him. Trump said Sunday he would welcome immigrants from certain countries but not Norway “because I didn’t get the Nobel Prize.” “So I don’t want anybody from Norway,” he said during the rally in the Michigan town of Port Huron ahead of crucial US midterm elections on November 3. There was no official indication of a new US policy on Norwegian immigrants. Norwegian Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide responded to Trump’s comments about the Nobel prize on Monday, maintaining that the committee is independent. “He knows very well that the Nobel Committee is independent. We have reminded him of that, in case anyone is wondering – and that is still the case,” he told national broadcaster NRK. Trump came under fire in 2018, during his first term, after using similar vulgar expressions to refer to Haiti and certain African countries. item.title: Ebola: Yobe Govt Activates Emergency Response Centres, Border Surveillance
item.description: The Yobe State government said it has not yet recorded any Ebola virus but has activated its Public Health Emergency Incident Management System and developed a comprehensive Emergency Preparedness and Response plan to monitor the possible outbreak of the disease. The Commissioner for Health, Dr. Mohammed Lawan Gana, represented by the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry, Hadiza Sabo, disclosed this while briefing journalists in Damaturu on Monday. According to her, the state government is building 6 technical pillars recommended by the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control for the Ebola Virus Disease response, which are coordinated through the Emergency Operations Centre (EOC). “Yobe State shares an international border; consequently, the state is strengthening cross-border surveillance and coordination with transport and relevant border authorities at key entry points to enhance vigilance, facilitate the timely detection and reporting of public health threats, and support prompt response to potential disease outbreaks” “We have outlined six pillars of coordination and management: epidemiology and surveillance, case management, infection prevention and control, laboratory services, communication and community engagement, as well as point of entry,” she said. Sabo further added that the government is intensifying public awareness campaigns using radio, television, community town carriers and engagement with traditional leaders. “Our message is simple; Ebola is real, but it is preventable and controllable. We are advising citizens to maintain good hand hygiene, avoid direct contact with the bodily fluids of anyone showing symptoms, and report any unusual illness or death to the nearest health facility immediately”. The government advises the general public to shun any rumours or misinformation and rely on verified information from the State Ministry of Health, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) and other official sources, and not to spread unverified reports on social media, as doing that can cause unnecessary panic and harm. item.title: Ebola: Plateau reactivates isolation centres, strengthens surveillance
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS – The Plateau State Government has reactivated isolation centres, intensified public awareness campaigns and strengthened disease surveillance as part of measures to prevent the spread of Ebola into the state. The state Commissioner for Health, Dr Nicholas Ba’amlong, disclosed this during a press briefing, saying the government had also directed its emergency preparedness team to assess safety measures at the airport and alert local government areas bordering neighbouring states. “Residents should maintain proper hygiene and avoid contact with potentially infected persons,” Ba’amlong said. “Maintain good hygiene, wash your hands regularly and avoid direct contact with the blood and body fluids of suspected infected persons,” he urged. “Remain vigilant and report suspected cases to health authorities,” the commissioner said, stressing that public cooperation was critical to preventing the spread of the disease.” ” The measures were announced alongside 10 resolutions approved at the 12th Plateau State Council on Health meeting held last week “ “The resolutions include establishing a state health trust fund, strengthening disease surveillance, addressing shortages of health workers and establishing an emergency fund for public health threats,” Ba’amlong said. He added, “These measures are aimed at strengthening the state’s preparedness to respond to disease outbreaks and improving the delivery of healthcare services to residents.” The commissioner urged residents to “follow public health guidance and report suspected cases promptly to health authorities.” The post Ebola: Plateau reactivates isolation centres, strengthens surveillance appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.description: Ahead of TenTrade’s “One Community, One Future” seminar on November 7th, we spoke with Andreas Andreou, Partner & Chief Revenue Officer; Obasi Wilfred, Regional Director, Africa; and Ademola Adeagbo, Head of Education, Africa. Together, they discuss what traders need to learn, how mentors can help and what building a trading community means in practice. Q: What does “One Community, One Future” mean to you? Andreas Andreou: It expresses the kind of company we want TenTrade to become. A global business needs more than a presence in different markets, it needs meaningful relationships within them. For us, bringing educators, mentors and traders together is part of building those relationships. Obasi Wilfred: For me, the important word is “community.” Our work in Africa has to reflect the people here, their questions, circumstances and ambitions. Community means having a two-way conversation and allowing what we hear locally to influence how we support traders. Ademola Adeagbo: I see it as creating an environment where learning is an ongoing conversation. You can attend a presentation and understand a concept, then struggle when you try to apply it. Having access to educators and mentors gives you somewhere to bring those questions. That is the value I want people to see. Q: Why Lagos, and why now? Andreas Andreou: If we want a lasting presence in Africa, we need to invest time in meeting people and understanding their expectations. Lagos gives us an opportunity to do that in person. Someone with more experience may understand those concepts but struggle to apply them consistently. My priority is to help people identify what they actually need to learn next. We should judge the value of the day by what it teaches us about the support people want next. Building a community takes consistent work. Obasi Wilfred: Regional relevance will determine whether people want to remain involved. If participants raise questions about their learning needs, those questions should inform our thinking after the seminar. We also need to recognise differences within Nigeria and across Africa as we develop that approach. A community becomes meaningful when people can see that their contribution matters. Ademola Adeagbo: Educationally, there needs to be a next step. Someone might leave realising that they need to understand something better or start reviewing their decisions more carefully. A useful learning community helps them pursue that next step and return with better questions. Q: What is the one thing you would like someone to take away from 7 November? Obasi Wilfred: The feeling that their perspective belongs in the conversation. We want our work in Nigeria and across Africa to be informed by the people we serve, and that starts with listening to them. Ademola Adeagbo: One practical habit: consider the potential loss before the potential return. If someone leaves with a better way to assess risk and a clear idea of what they need to learn next, that is a good outcome. item.title: AY apologises after payment dispute disrupts UK comedy show
item.description: By Wasiu Rokibat Nigerian comedian and actor Ayo Makun, popularly known as AY, has apologised to fans disappointed that the Cardiff leg of his “AY Live: Single and Not Searching” UK tour failed to go ahead as expected. The event, scheduled for Sunday, October 25, 2026, at Valegate Retail Park in Cardiff, Wales, reportedly saw hours of delays and confusion, leaving many ticket holders unable to see any of the advertised performers. AY, in a statement shared on Monday on Instagram, said he and the other comedians on the bill had travelled to Cardiff and arrived at the venue but could not perform because of unresolved payment commitments with the organisers. “My fellow comedians and I travelled to Cardiff to perform and eventually entered the venue. Unfortunately, unresolved payment commitments delayed our appearance, and by the time we arrived at the hall, most of the audience had left,” he said. The comedian expressed regret over the experience, acknowledging that fans who paid to attend the show deserved better treatment. “You deserved a properly organised show and timely information. You should never have been caught in the middle of a payment dispute,” AY stated. He also appealed to fans to hear his account of the incident before reaching conclusions about what transpired, saying he had explained the circumstances in a video. Addressing the issue of compensation, AY called on the organisers and the UK tour management to provide a clear resolution for affected ticket holders, including information on refunds. “I am calling on the organisers and our UK tour management to provide a clear resolution for ticket holders, including refund information,” he said, adding that verified updates would be communicated through his official channels. The incident had triggered complaints from attendees on social media, with reports of prolonged waiting, heated exchanges and police presence at the venue. As of the time of filing this report, the organisers had yet to publicly explain the circumstances surrounding the disruption or announce refund arrangements. This growing challenge for small and medium-sized businesses is why Trade Pathways, a US-based, student-run organisation, was founded. Its goal is to create opportunities for small businesses in Africa by giving them free access to the same clear, up-to-date picture of US trade policy that multinationals and large enterprises get from legal teams and policy experts. The platform tracks every US trade policy change and explains the structure in simple terms, so business owners can keep up with the constant shifts and understand buyer behaviour. Having initially served businesses in Kenya and Ghana, Trade Pathways is now launching full coverage for Nigeria, driven by recent trade policy changes and the potential adverse impacts on Nigerian business owners. “Small business owners should be spending their time making and selling great products, not on interpreting US government trade notices,” noted Keshav Suman, the platform’s founder. “The information is public, but it changes constantly and is written for lawyers and policy experts, not for the business owners it affects most.” The timing reflects growing activity among smaller Nigerian exporters. Non-oil exports reached a record $6.1 billion in 2025, and the Nigerian Export Promotion Council (NEPC) registered 1,129 new exporters during the year. NEPC’s Executive Director, Nonye Ayeni, has said the council is focused on “reducing dependence on large exporters by supporting small and medium-scale enterprises.” What Nigerian exporting businesses should know now Which party pays the tariff. The US import tax is paid by the American buyer when the goods arrive, not by the Nigerian supplier. Suppliers are still impacted indirectly, however, as buyers ask for lower prices, order smaller quantities, or move part of their orders to suppliers in countries that pay less. The exception is when a seller agrees to deliver goods with all import duties already paid, an arrangement that is common when shipping parcels directly to US customers. In that case, the seller would be responsible for the tax. Product classification. Exemptions from the new tax are set based on product and further classified by process, so two closely related goods can be treated very differently. Raw cashews, for example, are exempt, while roasted cashews are not. Before agreeing on a price, exporters should confirm exactly how their product is classified, so a buyer is not surprised by a higher cost after the order is placed. Refunds of the 2025 tariffs. The emergency tariffs the US charged on imports from around the world in 2025, including the 14 and 15 per cent rates on Nigerian goods, were ruled unlawful by the US Supreme Court in February 2026. US Customs has been refunding importers since April 2026, and on October 8, a US court ruled that importers who have not filed their own lawsuits are covered under a single group claim. Although refunds benefit US buyers, Nigerian export businesses that lowered prices to help buyers absorb the tariff can reasonably negotiate in future pricing discussions. AGOA and duty-free entry. The African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA), a US programme that removes the standard import tax on qualifying goods from sub-Saharan Africa, was extended in September 2026 and now runs until December 2028. It covers thousands of products, including several forms of clothing, footwear, leather goods, processed foods and wooden crafts. Nigeria has also been certified since 2005 to export handloomed and ethnic printed fabrics such as aso oke, Akwete cloth and Ankara prints under AGOA, a benefit that many business owners are not aware of. AGOA does not, however, cancel the new 12.5 per cent tax rate in place for Nigeria. US travel restrictions. Since January 2026, the US government has suspended new business and tourist visas for Nigerian nationals, which makes US trade shows difficult to attend. Video meetings, product samples sent ahead of a call, and US-based sales representatives or partners in the Nigerian diaspora can all help maintain buyer relationships through the absence of physical visits to the US. Alternative markets and customers. Selling to more than one market reduces the risk of depending on a single country’s trade rules. Europe is already Nigeria’s largest buyer of non-oil goods, and many Nigerian products receive reduced import taxes there. Since May 2026, China has charged no import tax on Nigerian goods, an arrangement that runs until April 2028, though food and agricultural exporters must still register with Chinese customs and meet its product standards. Closer to home, the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) is gradually lowering import taxes between African countries, opening regional markets that are often easier to reach than the US. What comes next Several US developments could change the picture in the coming months. American importers and 25 US states are challenging the current 12.5 per cent tariff in a US trade court, which heard the case on September 30. A potential ruling could reduce or remove the tax entirely, though an appeal is expected on either side. The US government is also expected to announce its annual decisions on which countries remain eligible for AGOA near the end of the year. Trade Pathways noted it is currently tracking each of these policy movements and will update guidance as announcements come. One such tool is a cost estimator, which calculates what a US buyer would pay at the border for a given product and shipment by country. The same shipment of wooden carvings costs about $1,297, almost all of it the 12.5 per cent tax. item.title: Plateau motorcycle rider killed, mutilated body found
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa A motorcycle rider has been killed by unknown assailants, with his mutilated body reportedly discovered along Longvel Road in Shendam Local Government Area of Plateau State. The victim’s motorcycle was also reportedly stolen, while the circumstances surrounding the killing remained unclear as of the time of filing this report. A resident of the community, Henry Homsuk, told newsmen that “Residents woke up on Monday to the disturbing news of the incident.” “It is sad that someone would be killed and his motorcycle carted away. We woke up to the news this morning, and it was disturbing,” Homsuk said. “It is painful that somebody would lose his life in such circumstances. We are worried about what happened and hope the authorities will take the matter seriously,” he added. ” The issue has been reported to security operatives,” he added “We appeal to the security agencies to investigate this matter thoroughly and ensure that those responsible are arrested.” ” People should be able to go about their lawful activities without fear,” Homsuk said. “Security should be strengthened along Longvel Road and in other vulnerable communities to protect lives and property and prevent a recurrence,” he added. Efforts to reach security operatives for confirmation of the incident were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report.
